newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures start lower in light trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures start lower in light trading.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened lower in light pit trading on Friday amidst heavy corporate debt supply and continued speculation of a coupon pass on Friday afternoon, both of which kept some traders on the sidelines.
December U.S. 30-year Treasury bond futures fell briefly through support at Thursday's overall low of 115-14/32, then rebounded at the 115-08/32 support level.

"There's not a whole lot going on down here. I guess that's the kind of day everybody's expecting," said one trader in the T-bonds pit. "We're not seeing any real flows today. It's just chopping around."
No key economic indicators are scheduled for release on Friday. October import/export prices will come out, but players minimized the data's potential impact on markets.

A Federal Reserve outright purchase of coupons could lend some support. The last pass in April 1996 came on a Friday at midday. Traders are expected to be watchful at that time on Friday for any signs of Fed activity.
One trader said market talk of a possible pass persists, but has not changed in some time. "That rumor's been out there for two weeks," he said.
